summary: Concurrent deployment induced 429s during priority-shard rollout for orchestrated workers
description: Issue summary: Customer FastLogix reports a sudden wave of 429 responses across multiple services after they triggered a staged rollout of our new priority-shard feature in their dedicated pool. Impact: Customer reported ~20% of interactive chat requests rejected with 429 over a 45 minute window; several business-critical webhooks also saw rejections causing downstream backpressure. Environment: dedicated pool in us-west-2, priority-shard rollout toggled via feature-flag 'priority-shard-v2' to 25% of routes, orchestrator version 1.12.3, ingress-proxy sidecar 2.3.1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Enable feature-flag for subset of routes (priority-shard-v2=25%) 2) Start orchestrated workers (100 parallel processes) performing mixed bulk + realtime calls to /v1/chat and /v1/embeddings 3) Observe 429s spike within ~3 minutes 4) Toggle feature flag off and observe gradual recovery Observed behavior: 429s include header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset: ~30s. Console shows per-route quotas decreasing for both new-shard and legacy routes simultaneously. Logs show many requests attributed to the same tenant but counted against multiple route buckets (duplicate token accounting). Expected behavior: rollout should route traffic to the new shard without double-counting tokens and without causing cross-route burst exhaustion. Attachments/links: Slack thread #support-fastlogix: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1670000000000, Ratecontroller PR referenced above, customer-provided request traces (attached to ticket).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated console, set priority-shard-v2=25% for org FastLogix 2) Launch 100 orchestrated worker processes which multiplex small chat calls (avg 40 tokens) and intermittent embedding calls 3) Monitor /v1/chat responses and rate-limit headers 4) Observe surge of 429 rejects within ~3 minutes

customer_impact_details: Customer reported degraded user experience for interactive chat widgets across their SaaS customers (approx 15-25% failed calls) and delayed webhook delivery for low-priority background jobs. They are on a dedicated reserved pool and require predictable throughput; this incident caused a business-impacting degradation and triggered their internal incident process.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: rollout introduced per-route bucket split but token accounting not yet synchronized between edge and origin, causing duplicate decrement.
- Observed correlation between feature-flag toggles and a spike in preflight/warmup traffic from orchestrated workers.
- Edge (ingress) was rewriting X-Forwarded-For and normalizing path prefixes; discovered recent proxy change (NGINX sidecar 2.3.1 -> config 'strip-route-prefix' enabled) that altered route fingerprinting.
- Ratecontroller logs show simultaneous debit to tenant and route buckets for same request ID in ~12% of sampled traces (duplicate-charge pattern).
- Related PR (ratecontroller#789) touched refill epoch rounding logic and priority-splatting; rolling re-deploy occurred earlier today and overlaps with customer's staged toggle.
- Reproduced in a canary by toggling feature-flag with a small orchestrator replica set; confirmed duplicate counting when proxy path normalization and shard split are enabled together.
- Confirmed that disabling 'strip-route-prefix' or disabling staged feature-flag prevents double-counting in the canary.

root_cause: A timing and attribution mismatch between ingress route fingerprinting (changed by sidecar config) and the ratecontroller's shard-splitting debit logic. When the priority-shard rollout was toggled, some requests were attributed to both legacy and new route buckets due to path normalization differences and a refill-epoch rounding race, causing tenant-level burst credits to be double-counted and producing 429 rejects.
resolution: Short-term mitigation: advised customer to disable the feature-flag (priority-shard-v2) and temporarily revert the sidecar 'strip-route-prefix' change if safe. Opened a hotfix PR that: 1) adds an atomic debit guard preventing the same request ID being debited twice across route shards, 2) strengthens route fingerprinting to use route-id + normalized-path digest, and 3) aligns refill epoch rounding to wall-time boundaries to avoid split-window debits. Deployed patch to canary cluster; after validation will schedule staged rollout across dedicated pools. Suggested customer configuration changes: route-isolation=true for priority lanes during rollout, and reduce orchestrator parallelism with a 10s splay between worker starts.
